items.topic: Layout shape for the standalone UI
items.context: The source UI (scenario-to-desktop) used a right-side Drawer that was opened from other contexts (records, smoke tests). In the standalone emulator UI there is no host drawer to anchor to — the surface is a top-level page. Research Finding 4 inventories the components but does not prescribe a layout. The choice drives whether we pull in react-router-dom and shapes the 'master-detail' interaction.

options.label: Master-detail: session list on the left, selected session viewer on the right (no router)
options.rationale: Single-page, no router, matches how operators actually use a session manager (pick from a list, work on one). Minimal new deps. 'Session list' view is concretely useful the moment a second session can be created.

options.label: Router-based: /sessions (list) and /sessions/:id (detail) via react-router-dom
options.rationale: Deep-linkable. Plays better with the future /embedded/emulator/external-url endpoint when it passes a session_id. Adds a dep and requires the vrooli-ui-interop slot [E] proxy-aware basename work.

options.label: Single active-session page, list pushed into a collapsible left rail
options.rationale: Preserves the scenario-to-desktop drawer-like feel (big VNC canvas, chrome minimized). No router. Slightly weaker discoverability of historical sessions.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own layout direction if none above fits.

items.notes: Recommendation is B because the next item in the chain (external-url endpoint) explicitly supports a session_id deep-link query param (conclusion Finding 9). Paying the router tax once in this item avoids a rewrite when the embed endpoint ships.

items.topic: Captures integration in the migrated UI
items.context: Research Finding 8 says capture *creation* is an emulator responsibility but capture *persistence* belongs to consumers. The existing liveDesktopStore depends on scenario-to-desktop's useCapturesStore to persist screenshots/recordings. When this UI moves to the emulator, that coupling is dead weight — there is no emulator-native captures store, and building one duplicates persistence responsibility.

options.label: Drop the captures store entirely; display capture results inline (e.g., last screenshot as a thumbnail) and let the user download the returned URL/path
options.rationale: Matches Finding 8's resolved design. Zero new persistence code in the emulator UI. The user still sees screenshots immediately after taking them.

options.label: Build a thin session-scoped captures list (in-memory only) so the user can flip through all captures from the current session
options.rationale: Slightly better UX for multi-capture debugging workflows, but adds a store with no persistence contract. Risk: operators expect persistence and are surprised when a refresh loses the list.

items.context: The migrated types are currently named DesktopSession, DesktopSessionConfig, DesktopControlsMenu, LiveDesktopDrawer, etc. In the new home (vrooli-emulator), 'desktop' is no longer the organizing concept — the scenario is generic session/display management with an eventual headless-session path. The existing names still read coherently; renaming has a real cost (all imports, all tests).

options.label: Rename aggressively: DesktopSession → Session, LiveDesktopDrawer → SessionViewer, DesktopControlsMenu → SessionControlsMenu, etc.
options.rationale: Matches the new scenario name and the /api/v1/sessions/ route. Cleaner for future readers who don't carry the scenario-to-desktop history.

options.label: Keep Desktop* naming for components, rename only the types (DesktopSession → Session) to match the API
options.rationale: Minimum-change approach. Preserves file names so git-blame still maps. Lower risk.

options.label: Keep all names exactly as they are
options.rationale: Zero churn. But leaves a naming mismatch with the /sessions/ API path forever — every future reader pays a small cognitive tax.

items.notes: Make sure not to leave around old names for compatibility. Should be hard cutover

items.topic: iframe-bridge event surface for this round
items.context: The item description calls out 'Integrate @vrooli/iframe-bridge as the child side.' The concrete question is which events to wire now vs defer to the phase-2 iframe-embed item. A smaller surface here means less rework when the actual consumer (scenario-to-desktop's future iframe embed) defines what it actually needs. A larger surface here means the consumer can drop in without a round-trip.

options.label: Minimal: init iframe-bridge with appId only. No custom events. Rely on built-in shortcut relay.
options.rationale: Lowest risk of event-schema drift against an unbuilt consumer. Defers the event contract to the phase-2 item that actually knows what the host needs.

options.label: Outbound lifecycle events only: session.created, session.state_changed, session.error, session.destroyed posted to the host on transitions
options.rationale: Gives the future host something useful (session awareness for routing/UI sync) without taking an opinion on host→child command semantics. Schema is easy to document.

options.label: Full bidirectional: outbound lifecycle events + inbound host commands (session.control.launch_app, session.control.screenshot, ...)
options.rationale: Most complete. But commits to a control protocol before the host (scenario-to-desktop's embed) has articulated what it needs. High risk of rework.

items.notes: Whichever option is picked, the contract must be documented in scenarios/vrooli-emulator/docs/embed-protocol.md (the chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation item will pick it up). Recommendation B keeps the contract small and auditable.

items.topic: Zustand store vs React Query for session state
items.context: The source liveDesktopStore.ts is a 192-line Zustand store that mixes local UI state (isOpen, error), server state (activeSession from GET /sessions/:id, metrics polling), and side-effect orchestration (heartbeat interval, VNC disconnect handling). react-coherence's state decision table is explicit: server state belongs in React Query; local UI state belongs in useState or a small Zustand slice. The migration is a natural time to split these.

options.label: Keep Zustand for everything (copy liveDesktopStore, rename, strip captures coupling)
options.rationale: Minimum migration risk. Known-good code path. But preserves the server-state-in-Zustand anti-pattern flagged by react-coherence.

options.label: Hybrid: React Query for the session list and session read, Zustand for local UI state (isOpen, connection status, error) and side-effect timers (heartbeat, metrics polling)
options.rationale: Aligns with react-coherence. React Query handles caching/invalidation for reads; Zustand handles the stuff it's actually good at. Medium migration cost.

options.label: React Query + plain useState/useReducer (no Zustand at all)
options.rationale: Lightest dep footprint. But the side-effect orchestration (heartbeat timers) is awkward without a store; would need a dedicated hook.

items.notes: Can split up zustand store if desirable

items.text: The emulator UI's main.tsx already satisfies vrooli-ui-interop slots [D] (iframe-bridge init) and [F]-partial (resolveApiBase in lib/api.ts). Migration work only needs to extend these, not introduce them.
vite.config.ts in the emulator UI correctly sets base: './' (slot [B]). No changes required to vite config for tunnel/proxy compatibility.

The emulator API's RegisterRoutes (api/livedesktop/handler.go:25-33) uses the exact /api/v1/sessions/ paths, so the rewritten API client becomes a mechanical find-and-replace on path literals in the migrated livedesktop.ts.
